The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. Job 01a15f18-70ae-72bf-8c8c-ba4110f88c79 completed with counts {"00": 50, "11": 50}. Only the correlated outcomes 00 and 11 appeared, which is the Bell pair result. The mock cost 0 credits.

The original circuit had two bugs.
1. It used QB25, but garnet has only 20 qubits (QB1 to QB20). I swapped QB25 for QB2. The live architecture lists QB1-QB2 as a calibrated cz pair. QB4 is the only other qubit that couples to QB1.
2. It used cx, which is not a native IQM gate. Garnet only accepts prx, cz and measure. I replaced the CNOT with its native form on the target qubit: prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, then cz on QB1 and QB2, then prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2.

I kept the first prx on QB1, which is Ry(pi/2) and creates the superposition. I also kept a single measure on QB1 and QB2 with key "m", so both qubits are measured.

The fixed circuit is saved at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-60/bell_fixed.json.
